content.body:
When the 232 was introduced, it was the most sophisticated wheeled vehicle in the world, with 8-wheel-drive and 8-wheel-steering, a fully independent suspension and a rear-facing driver for quick reverse escapes. They had exceptional off-road handling capabilities and were widely used for as long-range reconnaissance and command vehicles. The characteristic bed-frame antenna atop the 232 was for the Funkenwagen radio, and had a complicated mounting allowing the turret to turn freely.
The 232 was a successful vehicle, and the system proved its versatility in the later adoption of a number of variants. Among them was one with the short 75 mm cannon originally found on the Panzer IV D and the famed Puma Tank Destroyer with a long-barreled high velocity 50 mm gun. Its basic design, an 8 wheel mobile armored car with a light rapid firing gun mounted in a turret, is the same kind of specification used by most modern light infantry combat vehicles today.
The 232 remains an exceptionally mobile vehicle in World War II Online, although its top heavy nature makes it a little hard to handle and it can be rolled easily (careful on the curves and crossing steep slopes). Its speed, even cross country, means that a hard-pressed town can quickly be reinforced with swarms of 232s from bases even two or three towns distant. Despite its light armor, it can be infuriatingly hard to kill because so much of it is empty space inside. Enemies can pump round after round of AP into it, but if they do not happen to hit a crewman, engine, fuel or ammunition storage, they will not kill it easily.
When using the 232 in its recon role, remember to turn slightly to the right as you stop to view a forward subject because the antenna post can block the commander's view when at full magnification. The suspension on the 232 is excellent, firing on the move while at top-speed even moving cross country is quite effective.
Control Variations: Crew 2 no view slit.
